summary: A scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Meyers studied under Jay L. Garfield. She served as assistant professor and director of the MA program in Buddhist studies at Kathmandu University's Centre for Buddhist Studies at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Karin Preisendanz specializes in Indology and philosophy. She earned her Dr. phil. and Habilitation at the University of Hamburg. Her posts include positions at Freie Universität Berlin, the University of British Columbia, Hamburg, and Professor at the University of Vienna (1999).

A scholar in linguistics, Benary studied at Göttingen and Halle-Wittenberg, and under Franz Bopp. He served as a Gymnasiallehrer at Cöllnisches Gymnasium (1833–1860) and as a Privatdozent at Humboldt University of Berlin (1839).

An Indologist and linguist, Ammer earned his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna, studying under Geiger, Frauwallner, Trubetzkoy, and Havers. He held various posts at Vienna and served as professor and director at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from 1954.

Hase worked in linguistics and history. He studied at Jena, Helmstedt, and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. His career included roles at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, and professorships at the École Polytechnique, INALCO, and the University of Paris.

An Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, Seidenstücker studied at Göttingen, Halle-Wittenberg, and Leipzig (Ph.D.), working under Kielhorn, Pischel, Zachariae, and Ernst Windisch. He served as secretary of the Maha Bodhi Society and worked at Museum am Rothenbaum (1916).

A linguist, Bohnenberger earned his Ph.D. at the University of Tübingen, studying under Rudolf von Roth and Eduard Sievers. He worked as a librarian at Tübingen University Library (1888–1921) and held academic posts at Tübingen, becoming ordinary professor in 1921.

A linguist and Indologist, Brugmann earned his Ph.D. under Georg Curtius at Leipzig. He held professorships at the University of Freiburg (1884) and the University of Leipzig (1887–1919), where he succeeded Curtius.

Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Brunnhölzl studied under traditional teachers including Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, Tenga Rinpoche, Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche, Sangye Nyenpa Rinpoche, Ringu Tulku, and Khenpo Lama Thubten.

Specializing in Tibetology and history/archaeology, Debreczeny completed his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago under Hung Wu and studied under Jenny Purtle. He served as a curator at the Rubin Museum of Art (attested 2008).
Karl Dyroff was a scholar in linguistics and history/archaeology who attended Kronberg Gymnasium Aschaffenburg. He held a post at the University of Munich from approximately 1905 to 1938.

Zachariae von Lingenthal worked in history and archaeology. He studied at the Sächsisches Landesgymnasium Sankt Afra zu Meißen, Leipzig, Humboldt University of Berlin, and Heidelberg University, where he also held an academic post from approximately 1836 to 1845.

An Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, Neumann studied at Berlin, Halle-Wittenberg, and Leipzig (Ph.D.). His teachers included Paul Deussen, Wilhelm Grube, Albrecht Weber, Hermann Oldenberg, Ernst Windisch, and doctoral supervisor Richard Pischel.
Karl Felix Halm was a scholar in the fields of linguistics and history and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Munich and the Bavarian State Library from approximately 1856 to 1882.

Johansson was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Uppsala University under Olof August Danielsson and Per Persson. He spent his career at Uppsala University, serving as Privatdozent, acting Professor, eo. Professor, and finally Professor from 1908 to 1925.

Karl Florenz was a scholar of Japanology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig (Ph.D. under Ernst Windisch) and Berlin. He taught at the University of Tokyo (1889–1917) and held a chair at Hamburgisches Kolonialinstitut and University of Hamburg.

Burkhard specialized in Indology and linguistics, studying at Munich, Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Halle-Wittenberg (PhD), where he learned under Pott and Rödiger. He taught at Evangelisches Gymnasium Teschen and Akademisches Gymnasium Wien, later directing Franz-Joseph-Gymnasium Wien (1874–1890).

An Indologist and Iranian studies scholar, Geldner studied at Leipzig and Tübingen (Ph.D. under Rudolf von Roth). He held academic posts at Tübingen, Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, Humboldt University of Berlin, and the University of Marburg (1907–1921).

Hermann was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at Heidelberg under Friedrich Creuzer and Leipzig under Gottfried Hermann. He later held posts at Heidelberg University (~1826–1832), the University of Marburg (~1832–1842), and the University of Göttingen (~1842–1855).

Specializing in religious studies, Keil studied at the University of Tartu under Samuel Gottlieb Rudolf Henzi and Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp. He served as Privatdozent (1833) and Professor of Exegetics and Oriental Languages at Tartu (1838–1858).
